title: Clopen sections compute stalks and detect zero etale sheaves
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-pc-separably-closed], let $C$ be a commutative $K$-algebra, and put $E=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume that $K\to C_z$ is an isomorphism for every prime $z\subset C$, where $C_z$ denotes localization at the complement of $z$, and that clopen subsets form a basis of the topology of $E$. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on the small etale site of $E$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For each geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to E$ over $z$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the restriction maps induce a canonical isomorphism $$\varinjlim_{W\ni z,\ W\ \mathrm{clopen}}G(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\bar z},$$ where the transition maps are restriction to smaller clopen neighbourhoods and the geometric stalk is that of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The canonical germ map $G(E)\to G_{\bar z}$ is surjective; in particular $G(E)=0$ implies $G_{\bar z}=0$ for every geometric point. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$, every abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $T$, and every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, the canonical germ map $F(T)\to F_{\bar t}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03PN, section-stalks, geometric stalk definition; Tag 09AY, lemma-affine-only-closed-points; Tag 0EZV, lemma-check-stalks-better, finite-product presentation. Agent-written clopen stalk and germ-surjectivity refinement for the corrected proof.

proof.text: Fix $\bar z$ over $z$. Let $\mathcal A_z$ have the clopen neighbourhoods $W$ of $z$ as objects and inclusions as arrows. It is nonempty (it contains $E$), intersections give common refinements, and there is at most one arrow between any two objects, so it is cofiltered. The structural hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-clopen-etale-neighbourhood-cofinality] are exactly our hypotheses on $K$, $C$ and the clopen basis. Its pointed maps $W\to V$ give condition (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-cofiltered-criterion]. For condition (ii), take $W_1=W_2=W$ in its agreement assertion: the resulting inclusion $W_3\hookrightarrow W$ equalizes any two pointed maps from $W$ to the same $V$. Apply that criterion to the inclusion of $\mathcal A_z$ into pointed etale neighbourhoods and the functor $V\mapsto G(V)$ with values in abelian groups. By [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] the full colimit is $G_{\bar z}$. Thus the canonical map from the clopen colimit is an isomorphism. The criterion identifies its component on $G(W)$ with the germ at $(W,\bar z_W)$, so this is precisely the map in the statement, including its restriction transition maps.

proof.text: For any clopen $W\subseteq E$, put $W^c=E\setminus W$ with its open-subscheme structure. The inclusions of $W$ and $W^c$ are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and they are jointly surjective, hence a cover by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The empty covering and the sheaf equalizer condition of [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] give $G(\varnothing)=0$. Since $W\times_E W^c=\varnothing$, any $s\in G(W)$ and the zero section on $W^c$ agree on the mixed overlaps; on the self-overlaps they agree identically. The same equalizer condition therefore gives a unique $\widetilde s\in G(E)$ restricting to $s$ on $W$ and to zero on $W^c$. Uniqueness shows $\widetilde{s+s'}=\widetilde s+\widetilde{s'}$ and $\widetilde 0=0$. Thus extension by zero is a homomorphism $e_W:G(W)\to G(E)$ with restriction composed with $e_W$ equal to the identity.

proof.text: Let $g:G(E)\to G_{\bar z}$ be the canonical germ homomorphism. For each clopen neighbourhood $W$ of $z$, functoriality of germs gives $g\circ e_W(s)=s_{\bar z}$, by Step 2. Consequently every clopen-colimit coprojection has image contained in $H=\operatorname{im}g$. To see that $H=G_{\bar z}$ without assuming any extra colimit-preservation theorem, let $q:G_{\bar z}\to G_{\bar z}/H$ be the quotient homomorphism. Every coprojection followed by $q$ is zero. The colimit universal property from Step 1 implies that $q$ is the zero map; since $q$ is surjective its quotient is zero. Hence $H=G_{\bar z}$ and $g$ is surjective. If $G(E)=0$, this surjection has zero source, so $G_{\bar z}=0$. This applies independently to every geometric point.

source.place: Tag 03PN, section-stalks; Tag 040R, definition-stalk; agent-written clopen refinement of the setting in Tag 0EZV, lemma-check-stalks-better

proof.text: Finally take $C=K$ and $E=T=\operatorname{Spec}K$. A field has precisely the zero prime, its localization there is itself, and its one-point spectrum has a clopen basis. Step 1 applies to every abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $T$ and every geometric point $\bar t$. The only clopen neighbourhood of the unique point is $T$ itself, so the clopen diagram has just the object $F(T)$ and its identity map. Its colimit is $F(T)$, and the canonical isomorphism of Step 1 is the germ map $F(T)\to F_{\bar t}$. This proves the final clause even when $K$ is separably closed but not algebraically closed, and for arbitrary algebraically closed $\Omega$ in the geometric point.
